status: PROPOSED — NOT AUTHORIZED FOR EXPERIMENTAL EXECUTION
change_control: Any change to an arm, family, seed, subset, calibration, threshold, gate, margin, contrast, count or execution order after independent review requires a new versioned design (v3) recorded before any Phase-5 model fit; a reviewed version is never edited in place.

bootstrap.shared_draws: the frozen Phase-3.2/Phase-4 draws (same cohort, same draw identity) so every contrast is paired

inherits_unchanged.seed_aggregation: frozen R8 rule: per bootstrap replicate compute each seed's metric and average; no best-seed selection

source_validation_cohort.note: normal source-validation segments only; identical for S and T and for every modality

research_question: Under leakage-controlled Protocol B (few-shot split v3, Regimes S and T, frozen common test), and separately for RoboticArm and BrushlessMotor, does combining microphone, accelerometer and gyroscope evidence - by feature-level fusion (L1) or by source-validation-calibrated score averaging (L2) - change ranking discrimination, healthy-target false-alarm rate and anomaly recall at a frozen source-validation threshold relative to each matched single-modality detector; and, when one modality is lost, how much of that capability does an integrity-gated late fusion (L3) retain?

hypotheses.direction: two-sided for every contrast; no directional prior for or against fusion
hypotheses.H1: L2 (all three modalities) differs from each matched single modality (mic, acc, gyro individually) on the ranking axis and/or the operating axis.
hypotheses.H2: L1 (early fusion) differs from L2 (late fusion) when matched on family and seed.
hypotheses.H3: Under the loss of one modality, L3 (gated late fusion of the remaining two) retains or loses capability relative to intact L2.
hypotheses.null_reading: a contrast whose interval lies inside the pre-declared practical margin is reported as EQUIVALENT, not as a failure

estimand: Delta(metric) = metric(fusion arm) - metric(comparator) on the common test cohort, seed-averaged per replicate (R8), conditional on the observed evaluation cohort; 95% percentile interval from the shared paired class-stratified cluster bootstrap.
family_scope_rationale: All five Phase-4 families are retained so every fusion contrast is matched to an existing single-modality detector and conclusions can be checked for cross-family consistency. No family is added, removed or selected on the basis of Phase-4 protected performance.

L0_single_modality.status: EXISTS - completed Phase-4 protected benchmark; not retrained, not rescored
L0_single_modality.comparators: mic, acc and gyro individually, matched on machine, regime, family and seed
L0_single_modality.historical_best: the family-matched best Phase-4 modality is reported only as a labelled post-hoc historical benchmark (selected using previously observed protected results)

L1_feature_level_fusion.definition: one detector per unit trained on all three modalities jointly
L1_feature_level_fusion.classical_input: all 98 frozen Phase-3.1 segment-median features (mic 14 + acc 42 + gyro 42), train-only feature z-score; identical code, hyperparameters, seeds and threshold rule to the single-modality fits
L1_feature_level_fusion.statistical_reference_isolation_forest_o: REUSE the 28 Phase-3.2 all-channel detectors (already fitted, validated in reports/phase3_1/validation_only, and protected-scored in reports/phase3_2). A field-by-field comparison shows zero differences from the Phase-4 classical configs in split, split-manifest hash, preprocessing config, normalisation, threshold policy, aggregation, score direction, windowing and hyperparameters; same test cohort hash. Refitting would reproduce the same detectors and spend 28 duplicate looks.
L1_feature_level_fusion.mahalanobis_shrinkage: NEW FIT: LedoitWolf (assume_centered=false) on the 98 standardised features; score = squared Mahalanobis distance (1137-1555 training segments per unit; n/p >= 11.6)

dense_autoencoder.input: per-window concatenation [mic | acc | gyro] of the frozen Phase-4 log-power spectra from the same cache row (one window_id)
dense_autoencoder.standardisation: train-only per-bin z-score (equals the three Phase-4 per-modality standardisers concatenated; asserted in 5.2)
dense_autoencoder.architecture: frozen Phase-4 template d -> 256 -> 64 -> 16 -> 64 -> 256 -> d; ReLU hidden; linear output
dense_autoencoder.loss: plain MSE over all concatenated bins (naive; no modality re-weighting)
dense_autoencoder.training: Adam 1e-3, batch 256, <=200 epochs, patience 10 on source-validation window MSE, best-validation checkpoint; seeds 0-4
dense_autoencoder.capacity_note: one 16-d bottleneck for three modalities versus three 16-d bottlenecks in L2; accepted as the frozen recipe, reported as a limitation, not tuned

L1_feature_level_fusion.threshold: q90 (method higher) of the L1 detector's own source-validation segment scores

L2_score_level_fusion.definition: fixed rule over the frozen Phase-4 per-modality segment scores of the same machine, regime, family and seed; no model is trained or retrained
L2_score_level_fusion.seed_pairing: seed s of mic, acc and gyro are fused together (deterministic families use seed 0)
L2_score_level_fusion.calibration: per modality, robust z = (score - median_v) / IQR_v, where median_v and IQR_v are taken from that modality's frozen source-validation segment scores (normal source-validation only)
L2_score_level_fusion.pooling: arithmetic mean of the calibrated scores of the modalities in the subset
L2_score_level_fusion.threshold: q90 (method higher) of the fused source-validation scores of that exact subset; never inherited from a single modality
L2_score_level_fusion.missing_score: none expected (complete Phase-4 tables); a missing or non-finite per-modality score is a technical defect -> STOP, never imputed
L2_score_level_fusion.degenerate_scale: IQR_v == 0 for any modality is a technical defect -> STOP (checked in 5.3 on validation; not repaired by a fallback)

L3_sensor_integrity_fallback.definition: L2 mean fusion that excludes a modality whose raw signal fails a frozen integrity gate in that segment and decides with the source-validation q90 threshold of the surviving subset; an engineering safety/integrity rule, not learned sensor-reliability estimation
L3_sensor_integrity_fallback.identity_on_clean_input: when every modality passes the gate, L3 is identical to L2(all three) in score and decision

decision_policy.one modality invalid by a value failure: L2 of the surviving pair with that pair's validation q90 threshold
decision_policy.two modalities invalid by value failures: the surviving single modality's frozen Phase-4 detector and its frozen Phase-4 q90 threshold (decision-identical to the robust-z single-modality threshold, which is a monotone transform)
decision_policy.all three invalid: ABSTAIN_SENSOR_INVALID: no anomaly decision; segment retained and counted
decision_policy.any timestamp failure or absent modality: ABSTAIN_ALIGNMENT_FAILURE in v1 (see failure_types); segment retained and counted
decision_policy.integrity_flag: every segment carries its per-modality gate verdicts; any invalid modality raises an INTEGRITY_FLAG maintenance event independent of the anomaly decision, so a gated segment is never silently passed as healthy

L3_sensor_integrity_fallback.inference_class: frozen per-sample inference: every gate parameter is fixed before evaluation and the gate reads only that segment's own raw signal; no statistic is estimated from the protected cohort
L3_sensor_integrity_fallback.what_it_is_not: not sensor-quality estimation, not anomaly-novelty weighting, not a fault-versus-sensor-error classifier, and not evidence that clean readings are calibrated or free of subtle corruption

A_non_finite_values.gate_position: after loading, startup transforms and shared alignment (timestamps are valid, so the window grid is the clean grid); before modality-specific processing
A_non_finite_values.detection: G1 on the modality's samples within the common coverage
A_non_finite_values.survivors_processed: yes: startup transforms are value-independent (fixed initial accelerometer drop, time-based gyro warm-up) and alignment uses timestamps only, so surviving modalities see exactly the clean window grid
A_non_finite_values.survivor_scores: frozen Phase-4 per-modality transforms and detectors on the surviving modalities only; must equal their clean scores (bridging condition B2)
A_non_finite_values.threshold: validation q90 of the surviving subset

B_flatline_or_stuck_values.detection: G2 on the modality's samples within the common coverage
B_flatline_or_stuck_values.threshold: validation q90 of the surviving subset
B_flatline_or_stuck_values.v1_status: SUPPORTED (fallback); partial flatlines below 0.50 are not gated and degrade the modality's input silently

C_invalid_timestamps.detection: G3; the existing raw reader already raises on non-increasing timestamps, which the runner converts into a gate verdict rather than an unhandled error
C_invalid_timestamps.survivors_processed: no in v1: common_coverage takes start/end over all three modalities' timestamps, so a timestamp failure in one modality corrupts or blocks the window grid of every modality; recovery needs alignment over the surviving modalities only, which changes the window grid relative to the frozen three-sensor processing, so survivor scores would no longer equal the protected pair scores
C_invalid_timestamps.v1_status: ABSTAIN_ALIGNMENT_FAILURE; subset-aware alignment is out of first-stage scope

D_absent_modality.survivors_processed: no in v1: common_coverage requires all three modalities and raises otherwise

failure_types.multiple_failures: value failures in two modalities -> single surviving modality (frozen Phase-4 detector); three -> ABSTAIN_SENSOR_INVALID; any C or D failure -> ABSTAIN_ALIGNMENT_FAILURE regardless of the others

L3_sensor_integrity_fallback.what_the_pair_tables_measure: the detection capability, on clean protected data, of each two-sensor subset combined by the frozen L2 rule with that subset's own validation threshold

bridging_conditions.statement: The pair tables equal L3's output after a failure only if all of the following hold; each is development evidence, none is shown by the protected comparison itself
bridging_conditions.B1: the gate classifies the failed modality as invalid (development end-to-end suite, scenarios A and B)
bridging_conditions.B2: the surviving modalities' segment scores under the failure equal their clean scores (absolute difference <= 1e-9 for every frozen Phase-4 model)
bridging_conditions.B3: the runner selects the surviving subset's frozen validation threshold
bridging_conditions.B4: the failure is of type A or B; types C and D abstain in v1 and are not represented by the pair tables
bridging_conditions.B5: the surviving physical sensors are unaffected by whatever failed the other one (assumed; cannot be tested on this dataset)

L3_sensor_integrity_fallback.supported_claim: If B1-B4 hold in development, the protected pair results estimate L3's detection capability after a complete value failure (non-finite or flatline) of one modality, conditional on B5. They do not show resilience to timestamp failures, absent modalities, partial or subtle degradation, or real physical sensor failures.
L3_sensor_integrity_fallback.protected_realisation: L3 is not executed on protected inputs and no gate runs on protected data. Its protected evidence is the L2 all-three and L2 pair tables already in the matrix, interpreted under the bridging conditions.

integrity_gate.evaluated_on: each channel of the modality's raw stream after loading and the frozen value-independent startup transforms, restricted to the segment's common coverage [start, end) (pre-resampling, pre-normalisation)
order_of_operations: 1 load each modality; a missing or unreadable stream -> D
2 G3 per modality on timestamps (finite, strictly increasing, coverage >= 0.90 of the machine's nominal segment duration: RoboticArm 7.5 s, BrushlessMotor 5.2 s); any failure -> C
4 shared alignment over all three modalities (unchanged frozen rule)
5 G1 and G2 per modality on values inside the common coverage
6 surviving modalities processed and scored with the frozen Phase-4 transforms and detectors
7 robust-z calibration, mean over survivors, survivor-subset threshold, decision and integrity flag

rules.G1_non_finite: any NaN or +/-Inf value in any channel inside the common coverage -> modality invalid

G2_flatline.run: a maximal sequence of consecutive samples of one channel whose stored float64 values are exactly equal
G2_flatline.duration: t_last - t_first using that stream's own timestamps (not sample count x nominal period, because effective IMU rates vary by session)
G2_flatline.channel_flatline_fraction: samples in qualifying runs / samples of that channel inside the common coverage
G2_flatline.modality_rule: invalid if ANY channel's flatline fraction >= 0.50 (the frozen detectors consume all axes jointly, so one dead axis corrupts the modality input)
G2_flatline.quantisation_and_quiet_intervals: no exemption: the rule assumes a live sensor never holds an exactly equal stored value for 20 ms; this assumption is measured on every clean training and source-validation segment-channel (U1) rather than special-cased

rules.G3_timing: non-finite, non-increasing or duplicate timestamps, or own-stream coverage < 0.90 of nominal duration -> alignment failure (ABSTAIN in v1)

integrity_gate.parameters_fixed_a_priori: 0.020 s, 0.50 and 0.90 are fixed now from the physical definition of a dead or stuck sensor, not fitted
integrity_gate.clean_data_acceptance: every clean training and source-validation segment-channel of both machines (including released target-normal training segments and target-domain audio): zero G1/G2/G3 triggers -> otherwise STOP and report, no retuning. Report the full per-machine x sensor x channel distribution of flatline fraction and longest run; a sensor whose maximum clean flatline fraction exceeds 0.25 is labelled LOW-MARGIN in every later claim
integrity_gate.ambiguity_policy: the gate cannot distinguish a failed sensor from a genuine fault violent enough to saturate a channel for >= 50% of a segment; in that case the modality is excluded from the anomaly decision AND an INTEGRITY_FLAG is raised, so the segment is never silently passed as healthy
known_limits: a saturating genuine fault can be gated (false suppression of that modality's evidence)
one saturated axis gates the whole modality
partial flatlines < 0.50, gain error, bias drift, noise, timing jitter and miscalibration are not detected
the dataset audit (0 NaN, 0 Inf, 0 constant channels, 0 gaps, 0 non-monotonic timestamps) shows absence of gross integrity failures, not physical correctness of every reading
not_used: input-space distance to the training manifold
any statistic of the protected cohort

excluded_arms.reason: L3 is a gated mean, so L2-mean is its exact ablation; max pooling alarms whenever any single modality exceeds the fused threshold, so one failed or fooled sensor controls the decision by construction, and it degenerates completely under modality loss. Excluded for parsimony (would add 208 looks), not because of any Phase-4 result.
its statistic is the per-modality anomaly score in another form; down-weighting novel modalities suppresses the modality that is correctly detecting a fault. Not a reliability measure; rejected.
circular: on a fault visible in one modality only, the correct modality is the disagreeing one.
suggested in the Phase-4 report from observed protected results (microphone false alarms); adopting it would be outcome-driven selection.
changes the frozen source-validation threshold policy; a separate question for a later stage.

excluded_arms.arm: L1 pair models (early fusion of two modalities)
excluded_arms.reason: would require 52 x 3 = 156 new fits and looks; the pair question is answered by L2/L3 pairs built from genuinely trained single-modality detectors.
early fusion has no gating mechanism; evaluating it needs new inference on corrupted protected inputs and does not bear on the L3-versus-L2 question.

excluded_arms.arm: protected sensor-fault and additive-noise sweeps (research_definition section 13.3-13.4)
excluded_arms.reason: each corruption x severity x modality needs new inference of every affected detector on protected inputs (hundreds of looks); partial degradations are studied in development on validation data only (5.4) and protected sweeps are deferred to a possible later, separately designed stage.

excluded_arms.arm: new architectures (CNN, TCN, attention, learned fusion weights)
excluded_arms.reason: out of scope until the matched naive ladder is evaluated.

units.definition: machine x regime x family x seed

protected_tables.L3_clean: 0 separate tables: L3 is identical to L2(all three) when every sensor passes, and L3 is not executed on protected inputs

validation_only_operations.gate_clean_scans: all training and source-validation segment-channels, both machines
validation_only_operations.dead_input_constant_scores: 156 (one synthetic constant input per frozen Phase-4 model; no data)

protected_inference_operations.inputs: existing hash-verified common-evaluation spectral caches (20 dense-AE units) and common-test feature artifacts (4 Mahalanobis units), read only inside the authorized score-all scope after the exposure is recorded

accounting_definitions.new_model_inference: 24: a frozen L1-new model applied to protected inputs
accounting_definitions.derived_fusion_scoring: 208: a frozen L2 rule applied to sealed Phase-4 score tables; no raw-sensor inference

protected_data_reads.protected_inputs: common-evaluation spectral caches and common-test feature artifacts (for the 24 L1-new units only)
protected_data_reads.sealed_protected_outputs: the 156 Phase-4 score tables (to derive L2) and, in analyse-once only, the 28 Phase-3.2 score tables
protected_data_reads.not_read: raw common-test recordings (no protected gate scan)

accounting_definitions.reanalysis_of_existing_protected_outputs: 184 tables (156 Phase 4 + 28 Phase 3.2) used as comparators; no new detector meets the test labels, so no new look
accounting_definitions.new_protected_evaluation_units: 232 = one ledger row each = one new detector evaluated against protected outcomes
accounting_definitions.authorization: 1 human authorisation covering 1 batch of 232 units
accounting_definitions.completed_result: only after all 232 tables are persisted and hash-verified (completion gate GREEN) and analyse-once has finished; a ledger row records authorised exposure, not a completed result

outcomes.ranking_primary: AUROC on the complete common test

operating_primary.healthy_target_fpr: false-alarm rate on healthy target-domain segments at the frozen q90 threshold (lower is better)
operating_primary.recall: anomaly recall on the complete cohort at the frozen q90 threshold (higher is better)

reliability_outcomes.development: clean-scan trigger counts and margins; end-to-end suite criteria E0-E6; saturation characterisation; ungated-versus-gated validation FPR under synthetic modality loss
reliability_outcomes.protected: H3 contrasts (each L2 pair vs intact L2 all three) and each pair vs its two member modalities, interpreted as clean subset capability and, under B1-B5, as post-value-failure capability

interpretation.margin_rationale: Fixed by engineering judgement before any Phase-5 result and not derived from any Phase-4 effect size or variance: AUROC/AUPRC 0.02 is the smallest ranking change treated as practically relevant; healthy-target FPR 0.10 equals two of the 20 RoboticArm healthy target segments (the smallest change that is not a single segment); recall 0.05 is about 12 RoboticArm or 8 BrushlessMotor anomalies.

metric_category.order_of_evaluation: EQUIVALENT is tested first, then IMPROVEMENT/DEGRADATION, else INDETERMINATE
metric_category.EQUIVALENT: the entire 95% CI lies inside (-margin, +margin) (two one-sided tests at 2.5% each); annotated DETECTABLE_BUT_NEGLIGIBLE if the CI also excludes 0
metric_category.IMPROVEMENT: the 95% CI excludes 0 in the favourable direction and is not inside the margin; tagged MEANINGFUL if |point| >= margin, else BELOW_MARGIN
metric_category.DEGRADATION: the 95% CI excludes 0 in the unfavourable direction and is not inside the margin; tagged MEANINGFUL or BELOW_MARGIN as above
metric_category.INDETERMINATE: any other case (the CI contains 0 and crosses a margin), or fewer than 9000 valid bootstrap replicates; a small non-significant point estimate is INDETERMINATE, never EQUIVALENT

interpretation.ranking_axis: category of Delta AUROC (AUPRC and pAUROC are reported and any disagreement is flagged, never substituted)

operating_axis.O+: one of {healthy-target FPR, recall} IMPROVEMENT and the other IMPROVEMENT or EQUIVALENT
operating_axis.O-: one DEGRADATION and the other DEGRADATION or EQUIVALENT
operating_axis.O_tradeoff: one IMPROVEMENT and the other DEGRADATION
operating_axis.O?: otherwise (an INDETERMINATE component without a decisive conflict)

joint_categories.TRADE_OFF: (R IMPROVEMENT and O- or O_tradeoff) or (R DEGRADATION and O+) or (R EQUIVALENT and O_tradeoff)
joint_categories.UNDERPERFORMANCE: (R DEGRADATION and O-, O0 or O_tradeoff) or (R EQUIVALENT and O-)
joint_categories.INDETERMINATE: R INDETERMINATE or O?, reported with whichever axis is decisive
joint_categories.size_tags: every IMPROVEMENT/DEGRADATION carries its MEANINGFUL or BELOW_MARGIN tag into the joint category

interpretation.aggregation_across_families: descriptive robustness label only: per (machine, regime, contrast) the five family categories are reported side by side; CONSISTENT_ACROSS_FAMILIES when all five are non-contradicting on an axis, otherwise FAMILY_DEPENDENT; a family-dependent result is reported with each family's category and is never erased or averaged away

small_slice_rule.discreteness: RoboticArm healthy-target FPR moves in steps of 1/20 = 0.05 per seed (0.01 after averaging five seeds); the 0.10 margin is two segments; per-seed false-alarm counts k/20 are reported beside every interval
small_slice_rule.parent_uncertainty: the shared draws stratify by class only, so the number of the 6 healthy-target parents drawn varies by replicate and some replicates may contain none; such replicates are invalid for hFPR and counted
small_slice_rule.rules: RoboticArm operating results are labelled LOW-PRECISION; no RoboticArm operating claim from a point estimate; EQUIVALENT on RoboticArm hFPR requires the full CI inside +/-0.10, which is not expected with 6 parents, so INDETERMINATE is the anticipated honest outcome

interpretation.trade_off_rule: a TRADE_OFF is a finding, reported with both components; it is neither a success nor a failure of fusion

primary.P1: L2(all three) - each single modality (mic, acc, gyro individually); per machine x regime x family; AUROC, healthy-target FPR, recall
primary.P2: L1 - L2(all three); per machine x regime x family
primary.P3: L2(pair without m) - L2(all three) for m in {mic, acc, gyro}: the cost of losing modality m under gating

secondary.S2: L2(pair) - each of its two member modalities
secondary.S3: fusion arms vs the post-hoc historical best single modality (labelled post-hoc)
secondary.S4: source-slice and target-slice versions of every primary contrast
secondary.S5: AUPRC and pAUROC versions of every primary contrast
secondary.S6: T - S for every fusion arm

multiplicity.adjustment: none (percentile bootstrap tails cannot support Bonferroni-level quantiles from 10,000 replicates)
multiplicity.exact_primary_counts: P1 60 contrasts, P2 20, P3 60 = 140 primary contrasts x 3 primary metrics = 420 primary intervals
multiplicity.yardstick: the report states, per contrast family and metric, how many intervals exclude 0 next to the ~5% expected by chance under no true difference (intervals are correlated, so this is a reading aid, not a test)
multiplicity.language: each interval is reported as nominal; an isolated nominally supported contrast is never presented as a discovery; statements beyond a single contrast rest on the descriptive cross-family and cross-regime pattern

statistics.ranking_metric_intervals: reuse the Phase-4 family_bootstrap / paired-difference machinery and the shared draws
statistics.threshold_metric_intervals: NEW in 5.3: paired bootstrap of healthy-target FPR and recall differences with the same draws and the same R8 seed averaging (Phase 4 reported these as point estimates only)
statistics.valid_replicates: reported for every interval; < 9000 valid replicates -> INCONCLUSIVE

development_falsification.where: permitted training and source-validation recordings and synthetic inputs only; corrupted copies are written to a development directory; no protected data
development_falsification.physical_fault_evidence: none available: training and validation contain normals only. Synthetic fault-like perturbations are negative controls for gate behaviour, not substitutes for physical fault evidence
development_falsification.clean_scan: G1-G3 on every training and source-validation segment-channel of both machines; acceptance in integrity_gate.clean_data_acceptance

end_to_end_suite.exercises: raw loading, integrity detection, shared alignment, surviving-modality processing with frozen Phase-4 transforms, scoring with all 156 frozen Phase-4 detectors, robust-z calibration, subset threshold selection and the decision/abstention/flag output
end_to_end_suite.segments: 12 source-validation segments per machine, chosen deterministically: sort segment ids and take indices round(k * (n - 1) / 11) for k = 0..11

scenarios_per_modality.A1: NaN in all channels over 100% of coverage
scenarios_per_modality.B2: stuck at last value from 25% of coverage (75% flat)
scenarios_per_modality.B4: flatline over 40% (below the 0.50 trigger; expected valid; partial-degradation behaviour reported)
scenarios_per_modality.B5: plateau at the channel's extreme value over 60%

negative_controls_per_modality.N4: offset +3 training SD of the channel

saturation_characterisation_per_modality.S1-S4: gain x1.5, x2, x3, x5 then clip at full scale: accelerometer at the documented rail +/-15.988832 g; gyroscope and microphone at the clean-training maximum |value| of that machine-channel (an emulated full scale, because their physical full scale is not documented)
saturation_characterisation_per_modality.status: characterisation of the known suppression envelope, not pass/fail

pass_criteria.E0: clean runner scores reproduce each Phase-4 bundle's recorded validation scores within 1e-9 absolute (Phase-4 reproduction precedent 2.8e-14)
pass_criteria.E1: gate verdicts equal the scenario expectation: A1-A3, B1-B3, B5 -> modality invalid; B4 -> valid; C1-C4 and D1 -> alignment failure; M1, M2 as defined; N1-N9 -> all valid
pass_criteria.E2: for every A/B scenario, surviving-modality segment scores equal their clean scores (<= 1e-9 absolute) for every frozen Phase-4 detector (bridging condition B2)
pass_criteria.E3: the selected threshold is the surviving subset's frozen validation q90; two-survivor-failure decisions equal the surviving single modality's Phase-4 decision
pass_criteria.E4: C, D and M2 produce the defined ABSTAIN status, the segment is retained in the output and counted, and no exception escapes
pass_criteria.E5: clean and N1-N9 runs give L3 score and decision identical to L2(all three)
pass_criteria.E6: any unexpected exception is a software defect and fails the suite

end_to_end_suite.on_failure: STOP and report; no parameter is retuned; a revised gate is a new design version

development_falsification.ungated_failure_demonstration: descriptive: source-validation FPR of ungated L2(all three) when one modality is replaced by its dead-input score versus L3 (the surviving pair), per unit

protected_execution.inherits: Phase-4 score-all-then-analyse-once machinery, failure policy and provenance conventions; no second provenance framework
protected_execution.human_authorization: after the 5.5 freeze and an independent read-only audit, an explicit authorisation token stated by the human in chat and recorded in a pre-scoring identity record; authorized_protected_read is an accident guard, not an authorisation
protected_execution.execution_identity: clean tracked tree; scoring HEAD bound into the batch id; proposed batch id recorded at the freeze; authorised ids and cohort hashes must equal the proposed ones
protected_execution.read_scope: a single new protected script is the only additional opener of authorized_protected_read; it is added to the AUTHORIZED_SCOPES tripwire in the 5.5 freeze commit; the scope is an accident guard, not an authorisation
order: 1 pre-exposure verification on non-protected artifacts only: authorisation token, clean tracked tree, ledger == 196 and verify_ledger_history GREEN, every Phase-5 bundle/model/manifest hash, frozen design hash; no protected file is opened

2 record the exposure: append exactly 232 ledger rows atomically (batch=<id> in every reason) and write batch_authorization.json (batch_id, ledger_start_count 196, ledger_end_count 428, experiment_count 232, code_git_sha) and an attempt log entry EXPOSURE_RECORDED, all before any protected read

3 open the authorized read scope; verify protected integrity (common-evaluation cache and common-test artifact hashes, Phase-4 score-manifest payload and table hashes); a mismatch is a TECHNICAL failure after exposure

4 score the 24 L1-new tables from label-free protected inputs; derive the 208 L2 tables from the verified sealed Phase-4 tables; persist each table to sealed staging with its hash; log each unit's PERSISTED state
5 completion gate: 232 tables present, hashed, finite, label-free, ids equal to the authorised set
6 analyse-once: read labels and the 28 Phase-3.2 comparator tables inside the scope; compute every contrast, category and diagnostic once; final
protected_execution.ledger_semantics: one row per new protected evaluation unit (24 L1-new + 208 derived L2); re-analysis of the 156 Phase-4 and 28 Phase-3.2 tables adds no row; rows record authorised exposure, not completion
protected_execution.derived_table_provenance: each L2 table records the experiment ids and verified hashes of the Phase-4 tables it consumed, the calibration parameters and threshold from its validation bundle, and the rule version
protected_execution.manifest_hashes: pre_analysis_score_manifest_sha256, post_analysis_score_manifest_sha256 and score_payload_sha256 (canonical JSON excluding mutable status fields)
protected_execution.recalculation_guard: analyse-once refuses if an analysis directory exists; a completed analysis is final
protected_execution.failure_policy: see recovery and unit_states; inherits the Phase-4 rule that the same identity is never rerun and no metric is computed before all planned tables verify
protected_execution.ordering_change_from_phase4: Phase 4 materialised label-free test inputs before its ledger append; Phase 5 records the exposure first, so every protected read is attributable to a recorded authorisation

unit_states.EXPOSED: ledger row appended (looks consumed whether or not scoring completes)
unit_states.PERSISTED: score table written to sealed staging and hash-recorded
unit_states.FAILED_TECHNICAL: EXPOSED without a persisted table, with an attempt-log failure record
unit_states.COMPLETED: PERSISTED, completion gate GREEN and analyse-once finished

protected_execution.error_semantics: no integrity gate runs on protected data, so every exception in the protected batch is a TECHNICAL (software/infrastructure) failure; there is no protected outcome called sensor degradation in this design
protected_execution.attempt_log: append-only JSONL in the staging area: step, unit id, state transition, UTC time and code SHA for every step, including failures, so incomplete operations remain attributable

recovery.before_exposure: a refusal at step 1 consumes no look and needs no recovery record
recovery.after_exposure: looks are consumed; analyse-once refuses unless all 232 planned units are PERSISTED; an incident record names the failed units and cause
recovery.retained_units: units already PERSISTED with verified hashes are kept and never re-scored
recovery.recovery_batch: only FAILED_TECHNICAL units are re-attempted, under a new human authorisation, a new versioned batch id and new experiment ids (original id + '-r<k>'), appended as a new authorised ledger segment; a mapping file links each recovery id to its planned unit
recovery.duplicate_prevention: verify_ledger_history refuses a repeated experiment id; analyse-once refuses if any planned unit has zero or more than one PERSISTED table
recovery.no_retry_under_same_identity: the same experiment id is never scored twice

required_pre_5_3_hygiene: guarded loaders for both table families that require an authorized_protected_read scope before opening any file; refusal before open; a repository tripwire that fails if any src/ or scripts/ file other than the sanctioned loader module references those paths or reads them directly (including read_csv)
claim_boundary: Phase-4 aggregate protected results were observed before this design; Phase 5 is prospective in its frozen implementation but is not a pristine confirmatory test of fusion in general
results are per machine and per regime; no universal fusion claim
BrushlessMotor results are benchmark discrimination under brushless_motor_acquisition_time_class_confound_v1; a fusion gain there may reflect better session discrimination
RoboticArm operating results rest on 20 healthy target segments from 6 parents (LOW-PRECISION)
L3 is a sensor-integrity-aware fallback: an engineering rule for gross integrity failures, not learned reliability estimation; it is identical to L2 whenever all sensors pass
the pair tables measure clean subset capability; they estimate post-failure capability only for complete value failures (non-finite, flatline) under bridging conditions B1-B5
timestamp failures and absent modalities abstain in v1; partial flatlines, gain error, drift, noise, jitter and miscalibration are not detected
no physical sensor-fault evidence exists in the dataset; synthetic negative controls do not prove that genuine faults are never suppressed
unresolved_until_measured: U1: clean flatline-fraction distribution and margin per machine x sensor x channel (the audit rules out only fully constant channels); measured in 5.4
U2: RESOLVED - the Phase-3.1 validation-only thresholds equal the thresholds Phase 3.2 applied (28/28)
U3: whether IQR_v > 0 for every modality, family and seed; measured in 5.3
U4: L1 dense-AE training time and memory at 2918/2936 input dims; measured in 5.3

U5: valid-replicate counts for RoboticArm healthy-target FPR intervals with 6 parents; cannot be measured beforehand because the class-stratified draws depend on test labels; reported by analyse-once, and fewer than 9000 valid replicates gives INDETERMINATE
U6: whether the development runner reproduces every Phase-4 validation score within 1e-9 (criterion E0); measured in 5.4

implementation_stages.name: sealed-score-table guard (first), then fusion data assembly
matched naive fusion (L1-new fits, L2 calibration and thresholds, threshold-metric bootstrap)
L3 runner, clean scan and end-to-end corruption suite
pre-test freeze and protected script on fixtures
result report and ledger segment registration

supersedes.reason: independent review verdict YELLOW; focused corrections C1-C8; v1 is kept unchanged as the reviewed record under its own change-control rule

review_corrections.C1_L3_meaning: L3 renamed sensor-integrity-aware fallback; L3 == L2 whenever all sensors pass; pair tables measure clean subset capability, and the sensor-loss reading is conditional on development bridging evidence (arms.L3.bridging_conditions)
review_corrections.C2_end_to_end_feasibility: per-failure-type feasibility from the repository code (arms.L3.failure_types): value failures (non-finite, flatline) are recoverable on the unchanged shared window grid; timestamp failures and an absent modality break the shared alignment and ABSTAIN in v1; a development-only end-to-end corruption suite is specified (development_falsification.end_to_end_suite)
review_corrections.C3_no_test_dependent_gate: the protected raw gate scan is removed; no gate runs on protected inputs; exposure is recorded in the ledger before any protected read; every exception in the protected batch is a technical failure
review_corrections.C4_gate_false_suppression: exact G2 semantics (per channel, timestamp-measured 20 ms runs of exactly equal stored values, any-channel rule, no quantisation exemption, margin reporting, LOW-MARGIN flag); integrity flag always emitted; saturation emulation as characterisation, not proof
review_corrections.C5_statistics: EQUIVALENT only when the whole 95% CI lies inside the margin; statistically supported improvement/degradation tagged by size; INDETERMINATE otherwise; RoboticArm hFPR discreteness and parent uncertainty rules; unadjusted multiplicity handled by stated contrast counts, an expected-false-positive yardstick and nominal language; five-family consistency kept as a descriptive label only
review_corrections.C6_l1_matching: 28/28 units match on 17 recorded identities with 0 failures; no code drift in classical models, features, normalisation or the Phase-3.1 pipeline between 99f6055 and 85df48d; label MATCHED_BY_RECORDED_IDENTITY (l1_matching_evidence)
review_corrections.C7_accounting: explicit definitions of inference, derived scoring, protected reads, re-analysis, evaluation units, authorisation and completed results; state machine; partial-batch recovery and duplicate prevention (protected_execution)
review_corrections.C8_score_table_guard: sealed historical score tables guarded as the first 5.2 deliverable; development L2 uses synthetic fixture tables only; a separate authorised path for derived protected analysis (protected_score_access_policy)

l1_matching_evidence.method: for each of the 28 Phase-3.2 all-channel units and each of its three Phase-4 single-modality counterparts: frozen configs, Phase-3.1 validation-only bundles, Phase-4 pre-test bundles, Phase-3.2 provenance and ledger metadata; no historical score, metric or label was opened
checks: experiment id of the Phase-3.1 validation bundle equals the Phase-3.2 bundle id
machine, regime, family and seed (unit key)
score direction in threshold and config
source-validation segment ids of the score files
feature count 98 = mic + acc + gyro feature counts of the Phase-4 counterparts
the Phase-3.1 threshold equals the threshold Phase 3.2 applied (resolves U2)
top-level bootstrap configuration; feature representation (median_by_segment of the same 100 ms features)
l1_matching_evidence.earlier_checks_v1: split version, split-manifest hash, preprocessing config id and hash, normalisation strategy, threshold policy, aggregation rule, score direction, window and stride, metric and adaptation policy versions, and every model hyperparameter equal; same implementation version phase3.1-classical-baselines-v1
l1_matching_evidence.code_drift: git diff 99f6055..85df48d is empty for src/models/classical.py, src/features/extraction.py, src/preprocessing/normalization.py and src/experiment/phase31.py
l1_matching_evidence.common_test_identity: the ledger's test-cohort hash is identical for Phase 3.2 and Phase 4 on both machines; both read the same common-test feature artifacts
l1_matching_evidence.statistical_procedure: make_common_bootstrap_draws is a deterministic function of seed 1995, the cohort's segment ids, parents and classes; Phase-4 analysis imports the same routine, so identical cohorts give identical paired draws
l1_matching_evidence.label: MATCHED_BY_RECORDED_IDENTITY: equivalence is established from recorded configuration, cohort, contract and threshold identities and unchanged code, not by re-deriving or comparing fitted model objects
l1_matching_evidence.known_difference: input dimensionality is 98 versus 14/42/42 by design (that is the fusion contrast); nothing else differs

protected_score_access_policy.gap: sealed historical test score tables (reports/phase4_protected/staging/scores/*.csv, reports/phase3_2/experiments/*/scores.parquet) are readable by ordinary code; the Phase-5.0 guard covers test inputs only
protected_score_access_policy.first_5_2_deliverable: guarded loaders for both table families that require an authorized_protected_read scope before opening any file; refusal before open; a repository tripwire that fails if any src/ or scripts/ file other than the sanctioned loader module references those paths or reads them directly (including read_csv)
protected_score_access_policy.development_rule: L2 is developed and tested on source-validation scores and synthetic fixture tables only; no development code path may open a sealed test score table
protected_score_access_policy.authorised_path: the sealed tables are opened only by the Phase-5 protected script inside its scope, after the exposure is recorded (protected_execution.order step 3 onward)
protected_score_access_policy.acceptance: tests show refusal outside a scope with the real files present, no mutation, and that synthetic fixture tables load normally
